title: Eastern census and local-reception lane, batch 4: dated Dicastery tables of contents, Albanian and Piana catalogue leads, Hungarian copy provenance

uses.finding: OPAC SBN IT\ICCU\BVE\0501507 (Grottaferrata state library) catalogues an Albanian–Italian Chrysostom booklet, 55 p., [S.n.t.], [1979?], whose title names the Kisha katolike-bizantine e Shen Pjetrit, Elbasan. It is recorded as origin-review lead albanian-elbasan-mesha-hyjnore-sbn; the Albanian candidate slot stays empty. For census classification, the Dicastery's Oriente Cattolico Sommario (2017, ch. 34) and The Catholic East contents (2019, ch. 35) place the Apostolic Administration of Southern Albania among Eastern Catholics without their own hierarchy, with Russia/Harbin, Belarus, the ordinariates and (2019) Kazakhstan.
uses.limit: The booklet's title leaf, issuer, role (celebrant or people's book), approval, Greek exemplar and any use are uninspected; its bracketed date falls within Albania's 1967–1990 worship ban, so it cannot evidence celebration at Elbasan then. The Dicastery placement is a dated chapter grouping in a reference work, not a sui iuris ruling, personal-ascription decision or current 2026 census; it contrasts with the 2010 and November 2016 lists that name an Albanian Church.
uses.next_sources: Grottaferrata state-library copy of BVE0501507 (title, imprint, approbation, contents); The Catholic East (2019) ch. 35 text; ACCO Prot. 441/28 and other archival targets already recorded; a current named Annuario or Dicastery enumeration.

uses.disposition: unchanged-searched; dated celebration report added as source
uses.finding: katolici.mk post 44725 reports that Bishop Kiro Stojanov served the Chrysostom Liturgy at the Mother Teresa shrine, Skopje, on 11 January 2022. The Dicastery's 2017 Sommario lists the Apostolic Exarchate of Macedonia (ch. 27) and the 2019 contents the Eparchy of Strumica-Skopje (ch. 25).
uses.limit: The report names neither language nor book, so neither the 2009-approved Macedonian translation nor any edition is tied to the celebration. No title, imprint, approval leaf or exemplar of the reported 2009 Литургикон was found; COBISS was not retried because of its earlier proof-of-work challenge.
uses.next_sources: Original 2009 Литургикон title, imprint, approval and contents leaves; the 2024 jubilee monograph's publications section; a dated celebration report naming the book.

uses.finding: OPAC SBN PAL0225607 catalogues a 288-page trilingual Ieratikon co-published in 2006 by the Comune and the Eparchy of Piana degli Albanesi (editor Papas Jani Pecoraro; Arbëresh translation Giuseppe Schirò Di Maggio; Italian translation Tommaso Federici); the translator's bibliography (p. 3, image viewed) describes it as the Chrysostom and Basil liturgies with feast troparia and hymns. OPAC SBN PAL0225860 records a 1967 Greek–Albanian Liturgjia Hyjnore (catalogue title e atit tone shetrat Joan Hrysostomit) as published in Rome by the Associazione Cattolica Italiana per l'Oriente Cristiano, 182 p., with copies at Padua and Piana. OPAC SBN PAL0135089 records Paolo Schirò's 1964 Palermo Albanian Chrysostom translation.
uses.limit: None of these books was seen. The Piana Ieratikon's altar role, approval, Greek exemplar and parish use are unestablished, so it is an origin-review lead and not a documented Piana altar-book stage. The 1967 SBN record is compatible with the inspected Roma 1967 setting (spread 91 printed pp. 180–181) but not proved identical. Two SBN title queries found the Lungro Bollettino only as the 2012– series, so the 1968 decree issue was not located. Grottaferrata's 1960 Greek–Italian Chrysostom (SBN BVE1001462) was noted but not added (Italian layer deferred).
uses.next_sources: Piana 2006 Ieratikon title, approval and contents leaves and any introducing decree; Bollettino 3 (1968), pp. 14–16; Grottaferrata and Piana library shelf lists.

uses.finding: The Szent Atanáz college Corvina OPAC (106 subject-liturgikon long records read) has an undated possessor entry naming Fr. István Zolcsák of Nyírderzs for the 1646 copy M–920 (possibly recording only the 2010 transfer) and records the Nyírpazony Greek Catholic parish-office stamp at the catalogue locus 74. táblaoldal of the second 1646 copy; it transcribes a memorial note, written after 1881, recording that a Przemyśl 1840 Sluzhebnik was offered in 1856 for the use of the Sátoraljaújhely Greek Catholic church, a Mikóháza copy of that edition with inserted Hungarian translations, and a Lviv 1780 copy from Abaújszántó with manuscript references to Hungarian page numbers (Kótaj provenance for another copy). Two copy-provenance records were added; after cold review they are deferred origin-review records on the Hungarian route, not candidates. The OPAC also lists a Hungarian–Romani (Cerhari) Chrysostom liturgy with the cataloguer-supplied imprint [Nyíregyháza]: [Hajdúdorogi Egyházmegye], [2012].
uses.limit: All are catalogue transcriptions of ownership marks and notes; no original was inspected. The 1646 possessor entry and stamp are undated, so dated Nyírderzs ownership or use is still missing. The memorial note, written after 1881, reports an 1856 donation for church use, not approval or first celebration; the Hungarian page references are undated and their companion book unidentified. The 2012 Romani book is a deferred translation lead. No fuller 1646 copy, title or colophon image was found.
uses.next_sources: Szent Atanáz copies Ant10467, Ant10560, Ant30125, Ant30146 and Ant30101; a schematism dating Zolcsák's Nyírderzs incumbency; the Hajdúdorog circulars already listed.

uses.finding: The dated tables of contents of two official Dicastery reference works were obtained and inspected: the Oriente Cattolico Sommario (preface 1 December 2017; statistics from the Annuario Pontificio 2017) and The Catholic East contents (preface 14 October 2019). They group 6 patriarchal, 4 major archiepiscopal and 4 metropolitan chapters (5 Churches, Ethiopia and Eritrea sharing one), 9 chapters on Eastern eparchies and exarchates, and 4 (2017) or 5 (2019) on Eastern Catholics without their own hierarchy. Roberson's Annuario-based 2016 chart and 2017 tables give 19 Church or group headings without Albanian, Russian or Belarusian entries. Crosswalk: 20 of the 23 slots map to hierarchical chapters (Croatia-Serbia to Križevci plus Serbia; Ruthenian to the US metropolitan and Mukachevo chapters); Albanian, Russian and Belarusian map to the without-hierarchy section. The Czech exarchate, Kazakhstan, the ordinariates and Grottaferrata have chapters but no slot. The 2019 chart reuses the Annuario 2017 figures under a 2019 title.
uses.limit: Chapter headings are jurisdictions and categories, not a canonical list of Churches sui iuris, and neither work is a 2026 census. CNEWA's statistics pages returned HTTP 403, archive.org timed out, Google Books API returned a quota error and books.google.com an automated-traffic challenge (not attempted). The 23 slots are unchanged; a census of Churches is not a count of books.
uses.next_sources: Annuario Pontificio 2026 named section (print or authenticated digital); chapter 3 of Oriente Cattolico / The Catholic East on categories of Churches; a dated Dicastery list.

limits: No stage, transition or gap row was added: every new item rests on catalogue records, a translator's self-description, an official table of contents or a celebration report without a book, and the evidence rules allow those only as inventory leads or gap narrowing.
